Results.ReviewText:
I've had two of these now over the past decade and I do really like them. There are some significant design issues though. Most people complain that the grills don't get hot enough. The way they overcome this is by not putting vents on the lid and telling you to grill with the lid closed. This causes a different problem though. With no way to vent the heat, it is impossible to maintain a temperature below 475 degrees, way too hot for most grilling needs. So you either have to chose between it not getting hot enough with the lid open, or way too hot with the lid closed. They sent me a new regulator,  but that hasn't changed anything. 

The instructions say that it is normal to run too hot on first few usages, so they clearly know this is a problem and don't want you returning it. I think they presume that by writing that on there, they know you will keep it for a while in the hopes that it improves and then just never get around to returning it. A simple vent on the top of the lid that can be adjusted just like nearly every other grill sold has would solve this problem. So why haven't they added this yet? With that one little vent, this would be the perfect grill. 

The second design issue is the handle on the right side. You need two good handles for a heavy grill like, this but you can't actually use the handle on the right because the regulator is in the way. They've had these grills out for a while, no reason to not fix this by now. The third design issue I am a bit mixed on. The coated grills are nice in many ways and more durable than the cheap wire grills. But food sticks to it like crazy so it involves quite a bit of cleanup after each usage. 

So why am I still giving this four stars? I gave my last one to a friend who helped me move. I missed it for a couple of years and decided to spend 200 on this versus 40 for a cheaper portable grill. I just like the rugged look and feel to it. My last one was used at least weekly and stored on the back porch of a Colorado cabin. This is back home in Texas now, and I've got it installed outside on a homemade stand. For a single guy, this is a perfect size. It will grill for two quite easily while taking up a minimal space. I like that I can take it off the stand and toss it in the truck with a couple of one-pound bottles for visits with friends or hunting trips. I also like that I can plug it in with a basic 20 pound bottle on my home stand for daily use. But if I suddenly run out of propane, I could finish grilling with my camping bottles before I go and get a refill on the big bottle. 

Ultimately, I just like the thing. But I really, really wish they would fix these design faults. They would be so easy to fix and they've had plenty of time to do so. I'm tempted to find someone local who can just aftermarket install a top vent. That would make a huge difference.
Results.Title: Nice little grill but with some big design issues.

Results.ReviewText: Great little grill that is not too little!!!  Unfortunately, I did have to call Weber as my new grill had a defective regulator as verified by Weber Tech when I called at 8PM the night I put it together.  The lady tech had me to test to verify the problem and promptly stated they would be sending me a new regulator pronto.  It came 3 days later, I installed same day and was grilling 7 large pork chops for company dinner that night.  The  grill will cook a large amount for a so called small grill.  It has a great heavy duty cast iron grill.  The grill should always be preheated to around 400 degrees.  I did purchase the 1/2 cast iron griddle separately as the grill is in two pieces.  Do not put two griddles in you may overheat grill.  Remove 1/2 and replace with the griddle and start griddling after you season the griddle in the oven with canola oil wipe down after each heating.  Then will be the time for bacon, eggs, hash browns, pancakes and anything else you may choose to griddle.  In the case of my grill, if yours does not heat up to 400 degrees in about 15 minutes, (maybe less) call the Weber tech and they can get you going, and in my case a new regulator was the answer.  From my reading, a faulty new regulator is not uncommon on any brand of grill.  The Weber service is good and evidently 24 hours.  Bought for RV grill, but will be using far more than that.
